description: Scale instrument: a 123 x 24 serpentine maze, twelve elbows, twelve bodies.
notes: A room that does not fit on a screen, populated by a roster that does not fit in one convex cell. See `SERPENTINE_MAZE` above for the floor; this is what is standing on it.

Twelve bodies in one wave, spread one per corridor down the whole snake. That number is chosen against the *cost*, not against a difficulty curve: `sim/enemy.ts` calls `arenaNavigationTarget` once per closing enemy per tick, and that call only takes its cheap early exit when the enemy and the king share a convex cell. Spreading the roster is therefore what makes eleven of the twelve pay the full BFS and the full 13x13 portal matrix, every tick. A clump beside the player would test nothing.

The two archers stand at the foot of a leg with the corridor running away from them, because a 3-wide corridor is narrower than their 12-unit range: there is no sidestep out of the line, only retreat along it, and that keeps projectiles in flight across a long distance while the nav mesh is under load.
**Not a rung, not a hypothesis, and not balanced.** Whether this room is winnable is not the question being asked of it.
